title: The Debt of Marseille's old port
premise: Gideon Ishikawa, a financial-crimes investigator haunted by a night in Marseille she can't fully remember, is approached by a stranger named Camille who insists Gideon once saved her life — a favor Gideon has no memory of. The debt is real, however: Camille's employers, the laundering network that trained Gideon years ago before she turned informant, are calling in old obligations to force her back inside as they move a fortune through Frankfurt at market open. To protect Camille and finally sleep again, Gideon must burn the network from within, exposing the mentor who made her and paying the true price of survival: losing the clean life she built.
about_author: Hazel Galloway is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through Mediterranean ports before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers about people trapped between the ledgers they keep and the lives they owe.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In London, she works a routine fraud case with flawless precision but hasn't slept through the night since 'the incident' in Marseille three years ago. A postcard arrives from the Vieux-Port with no message, only a harbor stamp. Emotional beat: dread dressed as order.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A woman, Camille Roux, appears at her office claiming Gideon pulled her from the water off Marseille — a night Gideon cannot recall. Camille says her employers know, and that the debt must be repaid on their terms. Beat: vertigo; the past has a creditor.

chapters.title: Terms of Interest
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. She explains the network — Meridian — wants Gideon back for one job: validate a paper trail moving two billion euros through Frankfurt at Monday's open. Refusal means Camille pays the debt instead. Beat: coercion disguised as gratitude.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She digs into her own sealed informant file and finds gaps — redactions where her memory should be. Someone edited both the record and her recollection of that night. Beat: the horror of being an unreliable archive of yourself.

chapters.title: Vieux-Port
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Against protocol, she flies to Marseille and walks the harbor at dusk, triggering fragments: rain, a rope ladder, a scream under the quay. A watcher photographs her. Beat: homecoming as haunting.

chapters.title: The Trainer
chapters.summary: Anton Vey's POV. Introduced: Gideon's former mentor, elegant and patient, running Meridian's human infrastructure. He reviews her file and smiles at the redactions he ordered. Beat: menace through tenderness.

chapters.title: Recruitment, Again
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Vey offers her the Frankfurt validation personally, framing it as closure. He hints he knows what really happened the night Camille went into the water — and that it wasn't what Gideon thinks. Beat: temptation wrapped in paternal warmth.

chapters.title: Two Debts
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille confesses she was sent to recruit Gideon, but the near-drowning was real and unplanned — Meridian tested loyalty by nearly killing her. Her guilt curdles into alliance. Beat: betrayal becoming kinship.

chapters.title: Dry Run
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She agrees conditionally and audits a sample tranche, finding Meridian's new channel is brilliant — and built on templates she invented. They are using her own craftsmanship. Beat: violated authorship.

chapters.title: The Second Witness
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She tracks down Yusuf, a retired port clerk from the incident night, who reveals there was a second person in the water — someone who didn't survive. Beat: grief surfacing like a body.

chapters.title: Redaction
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Flashback threads assemble: Gideon's informant handler died that night; Vey staged it, and Gideon's memory was chemically blurred to keep her usable later. Beat: rage replacing shame.

chapters.title: Counterparty
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She contacts her old handler's successor at the agency, offering Meridian in exchange for protection for Camille. The successor wants proof by Monday open or nothing. Beat: bargaining with another kind of debt.

chapters.title: Frankfurt
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She arrives in Frankfurt embedded in Meridian's team, badge and all, playing the grateful returnee while mapping accounts, signatories, and the kill switch in the settlement flow. Beat: double life, held breath.

chapters.title: Audit Trail
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Left in Marseille, Camille discovers Meridian plans to erase Gideon after the transaction — the favor was always bait. She races to warn her. Beat: love outrunning fear.

chapters.title: Vey's Lesson
chapters.summary: Anton Vey's POV. Vey senses the turn and confronts Gideon gently, arguing that belonging was the real product he sold her — and that burning Meridian will leave her with nothing. Beat: the seduction of the cage.

chapters.title: Friday Night
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Preparations complete: she seeds the evidence, sets the exposure for 9:00 a.m. CET, and sleeps — actually sleeps — for the first time in three years. Beat: peace purchased at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the open, she triggers the disclosure cascade; regulators freeze the Frankfurt flows mid-settlement. Meridian's channels collapse publicly within ninety minutes. Beat: catharsis with a countdown.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Vey corners her in the parking structure; the confrontation turns violent, and Gideon survives only because Camille arrives — repaying the favor at last. Vey is taken alive, his empire testifying against itself. Beat: debts settled in blood and truth.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She gives evidence, surrendering her anonymity and her career's clean facade. The agency offers reinstatement; she declines. Beat: inheritance refused.

chapters.title: What Camille Owes
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille faces consequences for her role but receives leniency for her warning. She and Gideon meet outside the courthouse, neither owing the other anything now. Beat: freedom is frightening.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Back in London, Gideon archives the case, deletes nothing, and sleeps through the night — dreaming, for once, of the harbor in daylight. Beat: survival's price paid, belonging chosen.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: Epilogue, mixed POV. Months later, a small account surfaces in Singapore using Gideon's templates — Meridian's last cell, or a successor. Gideon and Camille look at each other over the printout. Beat: the past always charges interest; this time, they're ready.
